info.title: Milanko API
info.summary: Natural events + environmental variables for research
info.description:
Research API built on **NASA POWER**, **EONET v3**, and **NASA GIBS** (with FIRMS/AERONET/DONKI as complements).

### Method
- **Anomalies**: empirical percentiles by day of the year (±7 days, 2006+).
- **Event windows**: adaptive by category and duration, capped at 90 days.
- **Trends**: Mann–Kendall + Sen on seasonally adjusted monthly anomalies.
- **Correlations**: events/month vs monthly anomalies, lags −6…+6 and FDR (BH).

### Limits and notes
- POWER: max. 20 variables per request (the server splits them), **local solar time (LST)**.
- GIBS: quantifiable via WMS; thermal layers are vectorial (MVT).
- **Exploratory** results; the tool does not determine causality.

### Documentation
- Swagger UI: [`/docs`](/docs)
- ReDoc: [`/redoc`](/redoc)
- OpenAPI JSON: [`/openapi.json`](/openapi.json)

Python code: `core/nasa_events/` · Phase 0 results: `docs/00-recon/` · Analysis methodology: `docs/02-analysis/methodology.md`.

post.summary: Full analysis at a point: trends + events + correlations
post.description: Runs the Phase 2 pipeline in a single call: daily series, trends, per-event summaries (adaptive windows), and correlations with lags/FDR. If `events` is omitted, only trends are computed.

get.summary: Configuration to render the planet in the Milanko globe
get.description: Returns all the URLs and metadata the 3D globe needs: base binaries (ETDW), fine level, decoded cells, hexbinning, and GIBS snapshots.

get.summary: Metadata for the hexagonal geodesic grid (frequencies, sizes, biomes)
EONET events aggregated into hexagonal cells
get.description: Groups each event by its first geometry on the Milanko geodesic grid. Returns cell code, centroid, count, events, and magnitude totals. Use `format=geojson` for a FeatureCollection (point or polygon).

post.summary: Aggregates arbitrary points (with optional value) into hexagonal cells
post.description: Works with any research data that has coordinates: events, POWER observations, field samples… `aggregate` = count/sum/mean/max. If `geojson=true`, returns a FeatureCollection instead of the typed JSON.
